privacyNotice.committedToSecurity: Mae'r Weinyddiaeth Gyfiawnder (MoJ) wedi ymrwymo i ddiogelu a chadw eich gwybodaeth bersonol yn saff.
privacyNotice.describeHowAndWhy: Mae'r hysbysiad hwn yn disgrifio sut a phryd y defnyddir gwybodaeth o'r fath gennym. Mae'r hysbysiad preifatrwydd hwn yn disgrifio sut rydym yn casglu ac yn defnyddio gwybodaeth bersonol yn ystod ac ar ôl eich perthynas â ni, yn unol â chyfraith diogelu data. Caiff yr hysbysiad hwn ei ddiweddaru'n rheolaidd.
privacyNotice.typesOfPersonalData:
Math o ddata personol rydym yn ei brosesu

Ar hyn o bryd rydym yn casglu ac yn defnyddio'r wybodaeth ganlynol:

  • enw cyntaf y ddau riant neu ofalwyr
  • enwau cyntaf pob plentyn

Rydym yn casglu a phrosesu gwybodaeth sy'n ymwneud â chynllunio trefniadau plant i'ch helpu i greu cynllun trefniadau plant wedi'i addasu. Fodd bynnag, nid ydym yn casglu gwybodaeth sy'n eich adnabod yn bersonol (PII), fel enwau, cyfeiriadau neu fanylion cyswllt.

Gan nad ydym yn casglu gwybodaeth y gellir ei defnyddio i'ch adnabod chi, nid yw llawer o hawliau diogelu data yn berthnasol. Rydym yn eich annog i beidio cynnwys y math hyn o fanylion yn eich cynllun. Cyn belled nad ydych yn rhoi gwybodaeth na ofynnir amdani yn y gwasanaeth, nid ydym yn casglu digon o wybodaeth i wybod pwy ydych chi.

Gall y mathau o wybodaeth a gesglir gennym nad yw'n eich adnabod yn bersonol gynnwys:

  • manylion cyffredinol am drefniadau plant, fel trefniadau a ffefrir a lleoliadau casglu
  • cyswllt a ffefrir gennych
  • rhyngweithiad defnyddwyr gyda'n platfform, gan gynnwys ymddygiad llywio a defnydd nodwedd, i wella ein gwasanaeth
privacyNotice.howWeGetPersonalData:
Sut rydym yn cael eich data personol a pham ei fod gennym

Mae'r rhan fwyaf o'r wybodaeth bersonol rydym yn ei phrosesu yn cael ei darparu'n uniongyrchol gennych chi. Mae'r wybodaeth a ddarperir gennych yn cael ei defnyddio i lunio cynllun trefniadau plant y gallwch lawrlwytho a rhannu gyda'ch cyd-riant. Mae'r wybodaeth a ddarperir gennych yn caniatáu i ni drefnu'r cynllun yn seiliedig ar eich anghenion penodol, gan sicrhau ei fod yn adlewyrchu'r trefniadau a fwriedir gennych i'ch plant.

Mae casglu'r data hwn yn hanfodol i:

  • bersonoli'r cynllun ar gyfer eich sefyllfa rhianta
  • sicrhau bod dogfen y cynllun wedi'i lawrlwytho a lunir gennych yn cynnwys yr holl fanylion sydd eu hangen arnoch i gefnogi eich trefniadau cyd-rianta
  • darparu fersiwn o'r cynllun i chi y gellir ei lawrlwytho er mwyn gallu cyfeirio ato a'i rannu

Rydym ond yn casglu'r wybodaeth sy'n ofynnol i greu eich cynllun trefniadau plant ac nid ydym yn ei defnyddio at unrhyw ddiben arall heb eich caniatâd.

Nid ydym yn rhannu'r wybodaeth a ddarperir gennych gydag unrhyw sefydliad nac adran arall o'r llywodraeth. Defnyddir y manylion a roddir gennych i greu eich cynllun trefniadau plant ar gyfer creu eich dogfen cynllun wedi'i bersonoli i chi yn unig.

O dan Reoliad Diogelu Data Cyffredinol y DU (GDPR y DU), y seiliau cyfreithlon yr ydym yn dibynnu arnynt ar gyfer prosesu'r wybodaeth hon yw eich caniatâd chi. Gallwch dynnu eich caniatâd yn ôl ar unrhyw adeg. Y ffordd haws o wneud hyn yw dileu'r cwcis porwr. Mae yna wybodaeth am sut i wneud hyn yma.

Os ydych eisiau gofyn i ni ddileu eich data cwcis, cysylltwch â ni.

paperForm.title: Proposed child arrangements plan
paperForm.intro: Use this form from the Child Arrangements Plan service (https://propose-child-arrangements-plan.service.gov.uk/) on GOV.UK to collaborate to create child arrangements which you both agree on, without having to go to court.
paperForm.notLegallyBinding: Any plan you create using this service is not legally binding. The other parent does not have to do what it says and either of you can suggest changes to it at any time.

howToUseSteps.fillOut: Fill out the form saying what arrangements you would like
howToUseSteps.letOtherRespond: Let the other parent or carer add their response

yourSafety.title: Your safety
yourSafety.intro: You should only use this form if:

safetySteps.youAreConfident: you're confident that you and your ex-partner can make decisions together without putting yourself or the children in danger
safetySteps.doNotFeelPressured: both of you do not feel pressured or intimidated into responding

yourSafety.stopNow: If you have any concerns about safety, stop now.
yourSafety.feedbackOrSafetyConcerns: If you have any feedback or safety concerns about this service, you can email safety@propose-child-arrangements-plan.service.gov.uk.
yourSafety.cannotAnswerQuestions: We cannot answer any questions about child arrangement plans that have already been created.

howMakingChildArrangementsPlanHelp.title: How making a child arrangements plan can help
howMakingChildArrangementsPlanHelp.intro: You may find that collaborating with the other parent or carer on a child arrangements plan:

benefits.cheaperAndQuicker: is cheaper and quicker than going to court (it usually takes around 10 months to get a court order, depending on where you live and whether it’s urgent)
benefits.betterOutcome: leads to a better outcome for your children, which you and your ex-partner are in control of

howMakingChildArrangementsPlanHelp.goingToCourt: Going to court can sometimes mean you are not the ones who make the final decisions about your child arrangements.
howMakingChildArrangementsPlanHelp.tips: Tips to help you and your children

planShould.wishes: reflect the wishes, feelings and needs of the child
planShould.considerAnyHarm: consider any harm the child has suffered or any risk of harm

ifCourtOrderInPlace.title: If there is a court order in place
ifCourtOrderInPlace.doNotContinue: Do not continue if there’s a court order in place relating to you, the other parent, or the children.

orderList.protectiveOrder: protective order such as a non-molestation order, occupation order or a domestic abuse protection order
orderList.anyOther: any other order restricting contact between you and the other parent or the children

ifCourtOrderInPlace.toChangeOrEnforce: To change or enforce an existing child arrangements order, visit https://www.gov.uk/looking-after-children-divorce/change-or-enforce-an-order.

getMoreInformation.title: Get more information
getMoreInformation.moreInfo: Use GOV.UK to find more information, for example:

legalAdvice.title: If you want legal advice
legalAdvice.findLegalAdviser: You can find a legal adviser: https://www.gov.uk/find-legal-advice/find-legal-adviser.

domesticAbuse.title: Getting help with domestic abuse
domesticAbuse.signsAndEffects: To find out more about signs and effects of child abuse and neglect, visit https://www.nspcc.org.uk/what-is-child-abuse.
domesticAbuse.unsureVictim: If you’re unsure whether you’re a victim of domestic abuse, visit https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-abuse-how-to-get-help#recognise-domestic-abuse.

notSuitableForYou.title: This plan is not suitable for you if there has been:
notSuitableForYou.anyForm: any form of domestic abuse or violence, even if the abuse was not directed at the children
notSuitableForYou.drugsOrAlcohol: misuse of drugs, alcohol or other substances
notSuitableForYou.anyOtherSafety: any other safety or welfare concerns that place anyone at significant risk of harm

feedbackAndSupport.title: Feedback and support
feedbackAndSupport.toAskForHelp: To ask for help using this service, or suggest improvements, you can email feedback@propose-child-arrangements-plan.com.

notSuitableForYou.weCannotAnswer: We cannot answer any questions about child arrangement plans that have already been created.

childArrangementsProposal.title: About this child arrangements proposal
childArrangementsProposal.intro: Who this child arrangements proposal is for
childArrangementsProposal.careForChildren: The adults who will care for the children
childArrangementsProposal.answeringTheseQuestions: If you are answering these questions for someone else, enter their first name
childArrangementsProposal.otherParentFirstName: First name of the other parent or carer

livingAndVisiting.title: Living and visiting
livingAndVisiting.intro: Where will the children spend most of their time?

livingAndVisitingSteps.mostlyLiveWithYou: The children will mostly live with you
livingAndVisitingSteps.mostlyLiveWithOther: The children will mostly live with the other parent or carer
livingAndVisitingSteps.splitTime: They'll split time between both households

livingAndVisiting.tip: Tip: An exact split of time between two households does not always suit children's best interests.

scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.title: Which schedule best meets the children's needs?
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.intro: What timetable are you proposing for overnight stays, daytime visits and weekends at the other household?
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.commonSchedulesIntro: Here are some common schedules that can work well for children.
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.alternatingWeeksDescription: The children will spend one week in one household and the next week in the other.
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.schedule223Description: Children spend two days in one household, two days in the other, then back to the first house for 3 days including the weekend.
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.schedule443Description: Children spend three days in one household then four days in the other. The next week they switch.
scheduleMeetsChildrenNeeds.schedule2255Description: Children spend two days in one household, then two days in the other. After that they spend five days in one household, then five days in the other.

handoversAndHolidays.title: Handovers and holidays
handoversAndHolidays.intro: How will the children get between households?

handoverAndHolidaysList.otherCollects: The other parent or carer collects them

handoverLocation.title: Where does handover take place?
handoverLocation.intro: It may be easier for children if the handover takes place at a neutral location such as a park or railway station which you're confident you'll both feel safe in.

handoverLocationList.atOtherHome: At the other parent or carer's home

arrangementsSchoolHolidays.title: How will the arrangements be different in school holidays?
arrangementsSchoolHolidays.intro: School holidays include half terms, bank holidays and inset days.

itemsBetweenHouseholds.title: What items need to go between households?
itemsBetweenHouseholds.intro: Items include clothes, sports kit, school equipment, toys and electronics, medicines and personal care items such as toothbrushes.

specialDays.title: What will happen on special days?
specialDays.intro: Keep your children's needs and best interests at the centre of your plans for holidays and meaningful events. For example, New Year celebrations, Mother's Day and Father's Day, and birthdays.

otherThings.title: What other things matter to your children?
otherThings.intro: You may want to agree things such as:

otherThingsList.religionDietAndRules: religious practices, diet, and standard rules across both households
otherThingsList.extraCurriculars: extra-curricular activities, such as swimming lessons
otherThingsList.friendsAndFamily: access to other friends and family
otherThingsList.otherContact: other types of contact, such as video calls

decisionMaking.title: How should last-minute changes be communicated?
decisionMaking.intro: There will be times when plans will need to change, such as if one parent is suddenly unwell and cannot collect a child from school.

noticeForLongTermArrangements.title: How much notice should you give to change long-term arrangements?
noticeForLongTermArrangements.intro: Sometimes you may need to plan a long way ahead. For example, if you want to plan a holiday during time you do not usually spend with the children.

reviewingThePlan.title: When would you like to review this plan?
reviewingThePlan.intro: Children's needs change as they grow. When should you review this agreement to check it is still what's best for the children?
reviewingThePlan.youCanAlsoReview: You can also review these arrangements at an earlier time if they no longer meet your children's needs.

nextSteps.title: What to do next
nextSteps.addTheirResponse: Now give this proposed child arrangements plan to the other parent or carer so they can add their response.
nextSteps.collaborateToAgree: When they have added their response, you can collaborate to reach a shared agreement.
nextSteps.unableToAgree: If you are unable to make an agreement between yourselves, you could try mediation or another way of agreeing outside of court.
nextSteps.mediator: A mediator is a professional who will work with you to help you make decisions based on your child's best interests. They listen to both of you and take a neutral approach.
nextSteps.moreInformation: More information and support is available at: https://www.gov.uk/looking-after-children-divorce
